title: Protocol for high-throughput electron tomography exemplified on centrioles in primary human plasma cells
protocol: Prepare EM fixative according to the provided recipe.
Transfer a minimum of 100,000 live cells into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf protein LoBind tube.
Fill up the Eppendorf tube with 1× PBS.
Spin the cells down for 10 min at 1000 g and 4°C in a swing-out centrifuge.
Gently remove and discard supernatant, leaving the cell pellet slightly covered in liquid.
Add 1 mL of cold fixative to resuspend well.
Incubate at 20°C for 2 minutes.
Centrifuge again (swing-out, 10 min, 1000 g, 4°C).
Remove supernatant and add 1 mL of fixative to resuspend well.
Continue fixation in the fridge at 4°C for 12 hours.
Centrifuge the sample at 1000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and add 1 mL of 0.1 M cacodylate buffer (pH 7.4).
Store the sample in the refrigerator at 4°C.
Preheat a water bath to 37°C.
Heat a heating block to 37°C.
Prewarm a swing-out centrifuge to 37°C.
Melt low-melting-point agarose in a microwave (maximum 10 seconds) and keep it in the water bath at 37°C.
Cut off 4 mm of pipette tips for easier handling of low-melting-point agarose.
Preheat pipette tips and 200 μL PCR tubes on the heating block.
Stain cells by adding 50 μL of 20 mg/mL Evans Blue in 0.1 M cacodylate buffer to your sample.
Incubate at 20°C for 20 minutes.
Wash the sample 2–3 times until supernatant is almost clear and a blue pellet is visible on the bottom of the tube.
Centrifuge (swing-out, 10 min, 1000 g, 37°C).
Remove the supernatant and add 1 mL of 0.1 M cacodylate buffer.
Centrifuge again (swing-out, 10 min, 1000 g, 37°C).
Remove the supernatant completely.
Immediately add 150 μL of low-melting agarose to the sample.
Carefully resuspend once and place the mixture into a 200 μL PCR tube.
Centrifuge (swing-out, 10 min, 1000 g, 37°C).
Mix 4.5 mL of Epon mixture A with 10.5 mL of Epon mixture B in a 50 mL Falcon Tube.
Let the components mix for 30 minutes.
Add 0.225 mL of DMP-30 per 15 mL resin to the mixture.
Mix gently and do not shake to avoid air bubbles inside the resin.
Prepare different EPON concentrations (v/v%) in 100% acetone: 10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%.
Cut a PCR tube under the fume hood to free your cell pellet.
Add a few drops of 0.1 M cacodylate buffer to prevent dehydration.
Trim the pellet into small pieces with a scalpel if necessary.
Transfer the cell pellet or its pieces into a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 1 mL of 0.1 M cacodylate buffer.
Remove buffer and add 400 μL of 1% OsO4 in water to the sample.
Transfer samples into microwave and start the protocol.
When the microwave is finished, remove OsO4 from the samples.
Wash samples with dH2O twice.
Remove supernatant and add dH2O again.
Put into the microwave, continue protocol, then repeat this step once.
Remove supernatant and add 500 μL 1% uranyl acetate in dH2O.
Transfer samples into microwave and continue protocol.
Remove uranyl acetate and wash with dH2O twice.
Remove supernatant and add dH2O again.
Put into the microwave, continue protocol, then repeat this step once.
For dehydration, remove supernatant and add 50% acetone in water.
Transfer to the microwave and continue protocol.
Repeat steps with 70%, 90%, and 2 × 100% acetone to complete dehydration.
Transfer cell pellets into small glass vials containing enough 100% acetone to cover the pellet(s).
Remove acetone and start Epon embedding: Add 10% Epon in acetone, then put the sample in the microwave.
After microwave step, remove Epon.
Repeat steps with 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%, and 3 × 100% Epon concentrations.
Add the pellet(s) and enough Epon to an embedding mold.
Incubate at 20°C for 12 h.
Polymerize blocks in an oven at 60°C for 48 h.
Serially section Epon blocks and load onto formvar-coated grids.
Apply post-staining to enhance contrast in electron microscopy images.
Trim the block for sectioning.
Make serial sections of 200 nm thickness.
Place 5 or more consecutive sections on a formvar coated slot grid (2 × 1 mm).
Prepare one row of drops on parafilm for each grid: 50% methanol, 2% uranyl acetate in 70% methanol, and four 50% methanol drops.
Filter all solutions using a 0.22 μm filter prior to use.
Place the grid onto the first methanol drop.
Proceed to place the grid into the uranyl acetate solution for incubation.
Let the grid incubate in uranyl acetate for 5 minutes.
Rinse the grid through all four methanol drops, then place it in the first water drop.
Let sit in the water for 1 min with the lid on, then proceed to the next drop.
Repeat until last drop of water is reached.
Add potassium hydroxide (KOH) pellets to the parafilm.
Add one drop of lead citrate and cover with a lid for 2 min.
Add 4 drops of water next to lead citrate.
Place grid on lead citrate drop and incubate for 3 min with a lid on.
Transfer grid in first drop of water and let it sit in the water for 1 min with the lid on.
Proceed to the next drop until last drop of water is reached.
Transfer grid to a rubber plate with the sections facing upward.
Set up the electron microscope at 200 kV, cool it down and insert the grid.
Start SerialEM and load your settings.
Record a low-magnification overview of the whole grid at 80× to assess its quality.
Select 80× magnification in the Imaging states window.
Draw a polygon around all sections on the grid using ‘add polygon’ in the Navigator window.
Stop adding polygons by pressing ‘stop adding’ in the Navigator window.
Tick ‘Acquire (A)’ and ‘New File at item’.
Choose ‘Montaged images’ and ‘Fit montage to polygon’ in the upcoming dialogue, then press ‘OK’.
Select ‘Move stage instead of shifting image’, adjust the minimum overlap to 15%.
If necessary, increase overlap to 20% or higher if the acquired image montage is not assembled well.
Check that the microscope is in eucentric focus (‘Standard Focus’) when acquiring.
In the upcoming ‘File Properties’ dialog box, select ‘Unsigned integers’ and tick all information for storage in the extended header of the file.
Press ‘OK’ and save as ‘80_ov’.
Run ‘Navigator’ → ‘Acquire at items’, then select only ‘Acquire map image or montage’ and ‘Skip Z moves in initial move and Realign’.
Press ‘GO’ to start acquisition.
Label the new map in the Navigator window after acquisition.
Record an overview of the central section for image analysis at 400×.
Choose 'Unsigned integers' in the settings.
Tick all information to store it in the extended header.
Select 400× magnification in the Imaging States window.
Navigate to a corner of the central section from the 80× overview map.
Click on the selected area and press ‘Go to marker’.
Draw a polygon around the section for continuous mode mapping.
Record a map/montage as instructed.
Save the recorded map as '400_s3'.
Label your map in the Navigator window after acquisition.
Set up a reference map at 1000× magnification.
Use the 400× overview map to select a cell on an adjacent section.
Move the stage to this selected cell by clicking ‘Go to marker’.
Change to 1000× magnification in the Imaging states.
Adjust the beam and focus for optimal imaging.
Record an image of the reference area.
Save the recorded image as 'refmap'.
Click ‘New map’ in the Navigator window and label the new item as ‘refmap’.
Set ‘400_s3’ to ‘Acquire’ in the Navigator window.
Save the navigator as ‘nav.nav’.
Load your saved navigator file and double-check that ‘Reference map NavLabel’ is set to ‘refmap’.
Right-click on the ‘Image Viewer’ node, then click ‘Execute and View’.
Use ‘Model mode’ to create a polygon around the cells and omit section borders in 3dmod.
Save the model by pressing ‘s’ on your keyboard and close 3dmod.
Right-click ‘Interactive Segmentation View’ node, then click ‘Execute and View’.
Continue with step 46.h if content with the results.
Refer to troubleshooting for problem 2 if not satisfied with the results.
Right-click on ‘Python Script’ node, then click execute.
Open the new Navigator file in SerialEM: ‘Navigator’ → ‘Read and Open’ → select ‘nav_automaps.nav’.
Record an image at 1000× magnification and save it as ‘anchormaps.mrc’.
Click ‘New map’ in the Navigator window and label the new item as ‘anchormap’.
Tick ‘For anchorstate’ in the Navigator window for the new map.
Double-check that ‘anchormaps.mrc’ is the only open file in SerialEM.
Switch to 3000× magnification in the imaging states.
Check brightness and centering of the beam and apertures.
In the main window, click ‘File’ → ‘Open new’ → select ‘Series of TIFF files’.
Create a new folder ‘cells’ and in there, save your file as ‘c_’.
Adjust parameters for autofocus and eucentricity if necessary.
Click ‘Navigator’ → Acquire at items…’.
Choose the following settings: As ‘Primary Task’, tick ‘Run script’ and select ‘screen’.
Tick ‘Skip Z moves in initial move and Realign’ and ‘Turn off filament at end’.
Let the microscope run for the estimated run time.
Refill cooling agent (e.g., liquid nitrogen) as needed.
Use 3000× magnification images from previous steps to identify cells of interest using ImageJ software.
Discard all other items such as images of cells without interesting features.
Launch ImageJ on your PC.
Drag and drop the folder ‘cells’ into ImageJ.
Load the folder as a stack in ImageJ.
Check images for features of interest.
Note the image number of the target cell.
In SerialEM, prepare the Navigator file.
Set all polygons to ‘Acquire’ in the Navigator window.
Set all virtual maps to ‘Acquire’ in the Navigator window.
Set the reference map (‘refmap’) to ‘Acquire’.
Set all maps of cells without target features at both lower and higher magnification to ‘Acquire’.
Set all 3000× magnification maps (‘hm_xxx’) of cells containing target features to ‘Acquire’.
Set the ‘anchormap’ to ‘Acquire’.
Do not set 1000× magnification maps (‘lm_xxx’) of cells containing target features to ‘Acquire’.
Do not set the 400× magnification overview of the central section (‘400_s3’) to ‘Acquire’.
Save the Navigator file.
Save the Navigator file as ‘nav_prepared’.
Select ‘Tools’, then run ‘Delete Navigator’s Acquire Items’ in SerialEM.
Once the script is finished, re-open ‘nav_prepared’.
Check that all relevant data is still stored in the Navigator file.
Set up your microscope: Cool it down and load the grid.
Launch SerialEM and load your settings.
Open the Navigator file ‘nav_prepared’.
In the Navigator window, change ‘Registration’ to 2 using the arrow buttons.
Switch to 110× in the Imaging states.
Add a polygon around the whole grid in Preview mode.
Acquire a montaged image using the instructions from step 43.
Name it ‘ov_new’ and label the item in the Navigator window as well.
Open ‘ov_new’ and click on a corner of one of the outmost sections.
Navigate to this position by clicking ‘Go to marker’.
Draw a polygon around each section.
Set all polygons to ‘Acquire’ in the Navigator window.
Mark the first polygon in the Navigator window, then click ‘New file at item’ and ‘Montaged images’ with 15% overlap.
Choose MRC format and name the file ‘s1’.
Go to ‘Navigator’ → Acquire at items.
Select ‘Acquire map image or montage’ as Primary Task.
Tick ‘Skip Z moves’, then click ‘GO’.
Relabel the new maps in the Navigator file and save the Navigator.
Display your new image of the central section by double-clicking on it in the Navigator window.
Click ‘New window’ in the buffer control menu of the main window.
Double-click on ‘400_s3’. It will appear in your new window.
Arrange both windows so that they are displayed side by side.
Set registration points to shift the coordinates from the old items to the newly acquired ones.
Evenly distribute 6–8 pairs of corresponding points on the whole section.
Make them ‘registration points’ in the Navigator window.
Save the Navigator file, then save the Navigator as ‘s3_pretransform’.
Click 'Navigator' → 'Transform items'.
Record an image at 2300× magnification and save it as 'refmap_new'.
Label the recorded image as 'refmap' in the Navigator window.
Set all 1000× magnification maps (‘lmxxx’) to ‘Acquire’ and save the Navigator file.
Click ‘Tools’ → Update Microscope States for Selected Maps’.
Click ‘Navigator’ → ‘Read and Open’ and open the newly generated Navigator file.
Convert maps acquired at 1000× earlier into virtual maps at 2300× magnification.
Choose a virtual map in the Navigator window and click ‘Realign to item’.
Move the stage to a point on the central section.
In the main window, click ‘Task’ → ‘Eucentric Rough’.
Click ‘Navigator’ → ‘Acquire at items’.
Choose ‘Run script’ as a Primary Task and select the script ‘serial section_initial map’ from the drop-down menu.
Then click ‘GO’.
Compare newly acquired cell maps with virtual maps to verify correct identification of cells.
Refer to troubleshooting for problem 4 if an incorrect cell was targeted.
Click 'Add points' in the Navigator window to set points on your feature of interest, such as centrioles.
Rename points and add a section index.
Set all points to ‘Acquire’ in the main window.
Navigate to ‘Navigator’ → ‘Acquire at items’ and run the script ‘Name_pts’.
Tick ‘Skip initial stage move’ and ‘Skip initial Z move and realign’.
Click ‘GO’ and confirm the error message.
Rename all points according to the map they were added on, such as 'c001' for a point on 'lm001'.
Set all 2300× maps and corresponding points to ‘Acquire’.
Run the script ‘Add Section Index’ in the main window.
Edit the script accordingly in the ‘Scripts’ window if not screening on section 3.
Save the Navigator file.
Transfer acquired maps and coordinates to adjacent sections to locate target cells.
Duplicate the maps and points on the central section.
Shift the duplicates from the central section to another using transformation on low-magnification overviews of the respective sections.
Utilize the ‘RealignToItem’ feature in a SerialEM script to locate the exact cell and centriole point on the adjacent section.
Label the points automatically.
Mark the map ‘s3’ in the Navigator window and change its Registration to 3.
Display ‘s3’ side by side with the overview map of an adjacent section.
Add 6–8 pairs of registration points.
Change the registration of s3 back to ‘2’ using ‘Navigator’ → ‘Change registration’ in the main window.
Set the target points (the ones named ‘cxxx_s03’) to ‘Acquire’ and save the Navigator file.
Create a new Navigator file with the suffix ‘_duplicated’ by clicking ‘Tools’ → Duplicate Navigator’s Acquire Points and associated maps’.
Read and open the new Navigator file.
De-Acquire points from the central section in the Navigator file.
Find duplicated points at the bottom of the Navigator file and set them to Acquire.
Set registration back to ‘2’ using arrow keys in the Navigator window.
Save the Navigator file.
Click ‘Navigator’ → ‘Transform items’ in the main window.
If an error message appears, refer to troubleshooting for problem 3 and potential solution 1.
Check that 3 to 4 cells have been identified correctly by selecting a map or point in the Navigator window and clicking ‘Realign to Item’.
Refer to troubleshooting for problem 3 and potential solution 2 if results are not satisfactory.
In the ‘Scripts’ dialog, find the script ‘serialsections_pts_map’ and change the section number to the one just transferred.
Move the stage to a point on the adjacent section.
Click ‘Task’ → ‘Eucentric Rough’ in the main window.
Click 'Navigator'.
Run the script ‘serialsections_pts_map’ as a Primary Task.
Tick only ‘Skip initial Z moves and realign’.
Set the old virtual maps and the registration points to ‘Acquire’ in the Navigator window.
Save the Navigator file, then save as a new file (e.g., ‘s1_pretransform’).
In the main window, click ‘Tools’ → ‘Delete Navigator’s acquire items’.
Read and open the new Navigator file.
Repeat step 59 for all sections on the grid.
Sort the Navigator file by clicking 'Tools' → 'Sort Navigator'.
Browse through the sorted Navigator file to check all points were set correctly on all sections.
Use ‘Edit mode’ in the Navigator window to correct positions of any inaccurately set points or cells that were not imaged correctly.
Set all points to ‘Acquire’ and save the modified Navigator file.
Click ‘Tools’ → ‘Sort by Section’.
Switch to your desired magnification for tomography in the imaging states and adjust the beam as necessary.
Generate a new folder named ‘tomo’ and copy its file path.
Edit the script ‘quicktomo_master’ in the Scripts directory, pasting the file path to the newly created directory.
Set ‘realign to item’ (=1) as strategy in the edited script.
Check the available space on your hard drive: approximately 1 GB will be used per tomogram.
Start the acquisition by clicking ‘Navigator’ → ‘Acquire at items’.
Run the script ‘quicktomo_master’ as Primary Task, ticking options for ‘Skip initial Z move and realign’, ‘Close column valves at the end’, and ‘Turn off filament at end’.
Launch IMOD’s automated reconstruction through scripts on dedicated HPC hardware or use the etomo graphical user interface to manage the procedure.
Provide the location to the acquired tilt series and the batch directive with the reconstruction parameters.
During reconstruction, generate new ‘.rec’ files in the folder where original tilt series are stored.
Copy these ‘.rec’ files to a new folder called ‘reconstructed’.
Launch etomo and create a new join by clicking ‘File’, then ‘New’, then ‘Join Serial Tomograms’.
Set your working directory and name your output file.
Add all individual section tomograms of one cell in the ‘Join’ window.
Display each tomogram in 3dmod using the etomo graphical user interface.
Check the lower and higher frames for each tomogram.
Trim away frames without information by adding frame numbers in the ‘Start’ and ‘End’ panel.
Create a stack by clicking ‘Make samples’ and wait until the program has finished.
Calculate coarse or fine alignment, or manually align your stacks in the ‘Align’ window.
Once satisfied with alignment, switch to the ‘Join’ window and finish serial tomogram creation.
Display result directly from etomo or open it with IMOD.
